clue.text: Injured, too lame to become lovers

indicators.note: the fodder words are to turn into something else, so their letters are rearranged into a new phrase

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hurt and limping is told they will end up as a pair of sweethearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injured' looks like the anagram signal, but its letters are needed: 'to become' tells you to rearrange INJURED TOO LAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's star-crossed pair are the archetypal couple of young sweethearts.

clue.text: Story of upright type going to church

parts.note: roman is the upright printing typeface, as opposed to italic
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A printer's typeface is being taken along to a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a tale of love or adventure, a kind of story.

clue.text: Wrong idea of building on motorway south

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the building comes after the road and compass point

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords
construction is the act of building

explanation.surface: It is a mistaken notion to build on a motorway heading south.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway; its digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A misconstruction is a misunderstanding, a mistaken interpretation of something.

clue.text: Unbarred ring-fence

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
to pen is to fence in or enclose

explanation.surface: A gate stands unlocked in a fenced-off enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring-fence' reads as one word meaning to protect, but split it: ring gives O and fence gives PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbarred has had its bars removed, leaving it accessible and not shut.

clue.text: Northern kingdom in no manner accepting rupee

indicators.note: one piece takes in another, so the rupee goes inside the phrase meaning no manner

parts.note: in no manner means in no way
R is the abbreviation for the rupee, the Indian currency

explanation.surface: A northern realm refuses to take Indian money.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a Scandinavian monarchy in the far north of Europe.

clue.text: Ace banjo arrangement of an old king

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks a piece, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A virtuoso banjo version of a tune belonging to a long-dead monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacobean describes the reign of James I of England, a seventeenth-century monarch.

clue.text: Room for research into party speech

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the Labour Party
oratory is the art of public speaking

explanation.surface: A study of the way a political party makes its speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' is a link word here: the party leads into the speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a room equipped for scientific experiments and investigation.

clue.text: Ground-breaking can be terribly traumatic

definitions.meaning: read literally, breaking the ground, the earth, into pieces
figuratively, so shocking it seems to break your world apart

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground-breaking' usually means innovative; here it is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth-shattering means momentous and devastating, and literally describes smashing the ground.

clue.text: Way monkeys display bones in the ears

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
apes are primates, loosely called monkeys

explanation.surface: Primates on a road show off the tiny bones of their ears.
explanation.definitionFit: The stapes is the stirrup-shaped bone in the middle ear; the word serves as its own plural.

clue.text: Reportedly, one who needs a manipulator

definitions.text: Reportedly, one who needs a manipulator

parts.words: Reportedly, one who needs a manipulator
parts.note: heard aloud, needs is kneads: one who kneads muscles is a manipulator of the body

explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs' sounds like 'kneads', what a body therapist does to muscles; and such a therapist is a manipulator.
explanation.definitionFit: A massage therapist kneads and manipulates the body's muscles.

clue.text: Jazz-fan stripped in floor-show

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, so the word for stripped goes in the word for jazz fan

parts.note: cat is jazz slang for an enthusiast
stripped means bare, naked

explanation.surface: A jazz enthusiast strips off during a nightclub act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jazz-fan' reads as one compound, but 'cat' is jazz slang for an enthusiast, and 'stripped' is an adjective here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is entertainment performed in a nightclub while the audience dines or drinks.

clue.text: Refusal to approve niche

parts.note: no is a refusal
to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: Someone declines to sign off on a small recess.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small recess or sheltered corner, like a niche.

clue.text: Figaro's close-harmony style?

definitions.meaning: Figaro is the Barber of Seville, so his place is where he cuts hair
an unaccompanied four-part singing style with close chords

explanation.walkthrough: 'Figaro's' stands for Figaro's place, as one says 'the butcher's' for a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A barber's premises and the close-harmony quartet singing style share this name.

clue.text: New patient sick, short of potassium, commonly lacking spirit

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are formed into a different word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: lacking, so a letter is taken away from the word sick

parts.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A newly admitted ill patient seems flat and dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of potassium' drops K from SICK, leaving SIC; rearrange PATIENT plus SIC. 'Commonly' marks the everyday figurative sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In everyday use, something antiseptic is sterile in character: clinical, bland and without warmth or life.

clue.text: Stopping, getting rid of cold, and relaxing

indicators.note: a letter is removed from the word meaning stopping

parts.note: ceasing means stopping
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone stops work, shakes off a chill and unwinds.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing means loosening or relaxing, making less tight or tense.

clue.text: Dances of Indian girls — unchaste, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Indian dancing girls' performances are perhaps considered immodest.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautch is a traditional Indian dance performed by professional dancing girls.

clue.text: This college degree-angled, possibly?

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

indicators.note: possibly offers one rearrangement of the word angled

explanation.surface: A puzzle asks whether this college's name is a degree plus a slanted word.
explanation.walkthrough: Magdalen is an Oxford college; 'degree-angled' splits into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Magdalen College is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Amorous about teatime fiesta

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, so the amorous word surrounds the teatime one

parts.note: carnal means sexual, amorous
teatime is traditionally four o'clock, in Roman numerals IV

explanation.surface: Romance blossoms around teatime at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Teatime is taken as four o'clock, written in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a public festival with processions and merrymaking, like a fiesta.

clue.text: Word-game stuff boy does not finish

parts.note: to cram is to stuff full

indicators.note: the word boy stops short of its last letter

explanation.surface: A lad abandons a word-puzzle he was cramming for.
explanation.definitionFit: Crambo is an old rhyming game in which players find rhymes for a given word.

clue.text: Caught taking percentages for old cars

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
rates are charges expressed as percentages

explanation.surface: Someone is nabbed charging high interest on a deal involving cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is slang for an old, battered car or vehicle.

clue.text: Severely criticized, having hoarded silver inside

indicators.note: the silver goes within the word for hoarded

parts.note: saved means put by, hoarded
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A miser who stashed silver indoors was roundly condemned.
explanation.definitionFit: To savage is to attack fiercely, including in words, as a critic does.

clue.text: A name to describe a patron saint

parts.note: to describe a shape is to draw it; the past form drew is used

explanation.surface: A suitable name is sought to portray a protecting saint.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter takes 'describe' in its geometric sense, to draw; the past tense is loosely matched.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Andrew is the patron saint of Scotland.

clue.text: Said to be Noah's method of shipbuilding?

definitions.text: Said to be Noah's method of shipbuilding?

parts.words: Said to be Noah's method of shipbuilding?
parts.note: Noah built an ark; joining its metal would sound like a technique named after that vessel

explanation.walkthrough: Noah's boat was the Ark, and the joining method sounds like 'ark welding'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a technique joining metal using an electric arc's heat.

clue.text: Fuel undervalued to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the next word is taken, so the answer sits within it

explanation.surface: Fuel prices are partly too low.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is British slang for diesel fuel for road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv is diesel oil used as fuel for road vehicles.

clue.text: Schoolboy's warning can be hollow

definitions.meaning: Latin for beware, a British schoolboy's cry that a teacher is coming
a hollow in a hillside or underground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' (pronounced KAY-vee) is old British school slang for 'look out'.
explanation.definitionFit: The schoolboy's Latin cry for beware and an underground hollow share this spelling.

clue.text: City fashion

parts.note: a city whose name completes the phrase shipshape and ... fashion, meaning neat and in good order

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shipshape and Bristol fashion' is a British phrase meaning tidy; BRISTOL is a port city in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This English port city gave its name to a nautical phrase for good order.

clue.text: Undertaking course of study in university

definitions.meaning: in British usage one studies a subject at university by doing this, as in history
a university in the English town of the same name in Berkshire

explanation.walkthrough: British students 'read' a subject at university; Reading is also a town west of London with its own university.
explanation.definitionFit: Studying a subject at university and the Berkshire university town share this word.

clue.text: A new golden duck variety not recognized

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new type of golden duck has not been officially identified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like the anagram signal, but its letters are needed; 'variety' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unacknowledged has not been recognized or admitted.
